clue.text: Gold components used in circuits

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
bits are parts or components

explanation.surface: Gold parts are built into electronic circuitry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuits' reads as electronics, but it means laps or paths around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are the paths planets and satellites travel round and round, so they are circuits.

clue.text: A bit of a bad egg, and somewhat yellow, perhaps

definitions.text: A bit of a bad egg
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the white of a rotten egg, white gone off
second meaning: a pale shade tinged with cream or yellow

explanation.walkthrough: A bad egg is off, and one bit of it is the white.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white is a pale colour not quite white, often with a slight yellowish tint.

clue.text: Rugby players furthest away from the play?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the forwards at the rear of the scrum
second meaning: the last line of seats in a theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'the play' sounds like the game in progress, but it is a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the back row are the flankers and number eight; in a theatre it is the rearmost seats.

clue.text: Balanced reaction involving change of heart

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the phrase's two outer words differ only in their middle letter

explanation.walkthrough: Change the heart of TIT (its I) to A and you get TAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is an equal retaliation, giving back exactly what was received.

clue.text: Artist carrying back very old pie

indicators.note: carrying means the artist's name holds the next letters within it

parts.note: J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape painter

indicators.note: back means the letters for very and old are read the other way round

explanation.surface: A painter is carrying a very old pie back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns VO into OV, which goes inside TURNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a pastry folded over a filling, a kind of small fruit pie.

clue.text: Works holding up faulty units as not good enough

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the anagram sits above the works
faulty means the letters of units and as are broken and rearranged

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A plant is putting off defective items as substandard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as a verb and 'holding up' as delaying; in a down answer, holding up means sitting on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsatisfactory means falling short of the required standard.

clue.text: Monarch almost overthrown to create republic

indicators.note: overthrown means the shortened title is turned upside down, read backwards in a down light
almost means the last letter of the monarch's title is dropped

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, a reigning monarch

explanation.surface: A ruler nearly toppled, leaving a republic in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims REGINA to REGIN, and 'overthrown' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African state governed as a republic.

clue.text: Medicinal plant short-lived king used without success?

indicators.note: used signals placing the king inside the next piece, as in vain he was in vain

parts.note: in vain means without success; the king is put in vain
Edward V reigned only weeks in 1483 before vanishing; Edward is ER and the numeral is V

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy is tried on a briefly reigning king, to no effect.
explanation.walkthrough: ER V is Edward V, one of the Princes in the Tower; he is put in VAIN, which is what 'without success' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Vervain is the herb verbena, long used in folk medicine for many ailments.

clue.text: Cheap drink provided by fly-by-night operator?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: American slang for rough cheap whisky
second meaning: an overnight flight, one that flies by night

explanation.walkthrough: A fly-by-night operator is normally a dodgy trader; here it is read literally as a night flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-eye is both poor-quality whisky and an overnight flight that leaves passengers bleary.

clue.text: Early meeting of consumers quickly following electricity cut

indicators.note: following means the word for quickly comes after the cut

parts.note: a power break is an interruption to the electricity supply
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: Customers gather early after a sudden blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumers' are people eating, not shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A power breakfast is a business meeting held over the morning meal.

clue.text: Divided about drug being not serious

indicators.note: about means the word for divided goes round the drug's letter

parts.note: factious means split into quarrelling factions
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A split group argue about a drug, unable to take things seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious remarks are flippant jokes made where gravity is expected.

clue.text: Politician and his party damaged by charge

parts.note: Al Gore, the former US Vice-President
D stands for Democrat, Gore's party

explanation.surface: A politician and his party are hurt by an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an accusation, but it is a bull's charge with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gored is to be pierced by horns, the injury from a bull rushing at someone.

clue.text: Take a lot of cash or money for messenger released from cell

indicators.note: taking a lot of the phrase means using most of its letters, a run inside the words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of cash, through or, into money

explanation.surface: Someone is grabbing a pile of cash or money for a messenger freed from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The cell sounds like a prison cell, but it is a biological one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hormone is a chemical signal secreted by cells and carried in the blood to act elsewhere.

clue.text: Eastern region in which sailors reach journey's end

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, so two of them give tar twice

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of journey's

parts.note: its last letter is Y

explanation.surface: Sailors reach the end of their voyage in some eastern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartary was the historic European name for the vast lands of central and northern Asia.

clue.text: I.e. get that vehicle out of here!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: that is to say, the sense of id est

definitions.text: get that vehicle out of here!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., an order to haul the car away

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as TOW IT, what a parking warden might say.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is an old phrase introducing an explanation, just as id est does.

clue.text: Point from which to start or end in court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reference level from which change is measured
second meaning: the line marking the far end of a tennis court

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' hints at law, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseline is both a starting reference for measurement and the back line of a tennis court.

clue.text: Illegally attacking with weapon more powerful than sword

definitions.text: Illegally attacking with weapon more powerful than sword

parts.words: Illegally attacking with weapon more powerful than sword
parts.note: the pen is mightier than the sword, so this is an unlawful attack in writing

explanation.walkthrough: The weapon is the pen, from the saying that the pen is mightier than the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Libellous writing damages someone's reputation with false statements in print, which is unlawful.

clue.text: A friend with medical degree making inventions such as laser

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
MS is a Master of Surgery degree

explanation.surface: A friend with a doctor's qualification comes up with devices like lasers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laser' looks like a gadget, but here it is the word formed from initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Laser was coined from the initials of a longer phrase, which makes it an acronym.

clue.text: Curse old woman put on every article

indicators.note: put on means the old woman's letters are attached after the articles

parts.note: the English articles an, a and the, all of them in turn
ma is slang for mother

explanation.surface: A curse is laid on every item by an old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every article' is a grammar joke: AN, A and THE are all the articles English has.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal curse of excommunication, and by extension something loathed.

clue.text: Something sweet, meaning love

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from sweet ..., tender words
second meaning: zero, as in a tennis score

explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love means zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing is zero, which tennis calls love, and sweet nothing is an affectionate whisper.

clue.text: Educational achievement, so elementary

parts.note: BA, a Bachelor of Arts degree
sic is Latin for thus or so, used in quotations

explanation.surface: Getting a qualification is, so it seems, quite elementary.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and elementary are synonyms for simple and fundamental.

clue.text: One who dishonestly advocates taking part in mass hysteria

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crooked campaigner joins in a wave of public panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer, one who argues cases by sharp practice.

clue.text: Well-behaved, over time, like all of us

indicators.note: over means the word for well-behaved spreads over the time letter, covering it

parts.note: moral means virtuous and well-behaved

explanation.surface: Good conduct over a period is what makes us human.
explanation.definitionFit: Every human is mortal, bound to die eventually.

clue.text: Remote area revealed to be better

parts.note: out means made public or revealed
a better is one who bets, and to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: A distant spot turns out to be superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good, but it is someone placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Outback is the sparsely populated interior of Australia.

clue.text: In accordance with the rules, first sent off for foul

indicators.note: first sent off means the opening letter is removed, like a player dismissed

parts.note: lawful means permitted by the rules

explanation.surface: A player is fairly dismissed first for a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface of 'sent off for foul' hides that foul is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and foul both mean very bad or unpleasant.

clue.text: Some brutally honest call that leads to a death

definitions.text: call that leads to a death

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some blunt frankness is a remark that brings about someone's end.
explanation.walkthrough: The death is a fox's: the huntsman's cry starts the chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the hunting cry raised when the fox is sighted, setting the hounds after it.

clue.text: The force needs to put one inside

definitions.text: The force needs to put one inside

indicators.note: needs to put says the next piece is placed into the letters before
inside says that piece goes within, not beside

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: The police must lock somebody up.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the criminal the police want behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is a criminal the police aim to jail, putting him inside prison.

clue.text: Like a well-made kite, suitable for Auntie?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC, so fit to put on air

explanation.walkthrough: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is a British nickname for the BBC; worth airing is fit to broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Airworthy describes a craft safe to fly, and here also programmes worth broadcasting.

clue.text: Valid status of cricket side settled before close of play

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
alit means landed or settled

indicators.note: close of points to the final letter of play

parts.note: its last letter is Y

explanation.surface: A cricket team's standing is decided before stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Legality is the state of being lawful, a valid standing in law.

clue.text: Old star you heard has gone — he was worshipped at one time

definitions.text: he was worshipped at one time

indicators.note: has gone means a letter is dropped from the star's name

parts.note: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky

indicators.note: heard says the word you is taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: An ageing celebrity has left the scene, but he was once adored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a celebrity, but it is SIRIUS losing the U ('you heard').
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian god of the dead, revered for millennia.
